To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cerebral hemoglobin oxygenation and the Cyt.ox./Cyt.redox state were changed during and after seizure in the rat.
the cerebral oxygenation state during and after seizure was measured by using near infrared spectropho-tometry.
the Cyt.ox.-reducing state during seizure and the CBF increase during seizure are closely related to each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hemodynamic changes in the cerebral cortex during chemically-induced seizures and their effects on cerebral oxygenation state.
the relationship between cerebral hemodynamic changes and the cerebral oxygenation state during seizure.
the relationship between cerebral oxygenation state and CBF during and after chemically-induced seizures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hemoglobin oxygenation and Cyt.ox.redox states are closely related to the CBF and cerebral metabolism during seizure and in post-ictal phase.
the CBF and Cyt.ox., which are the main targets of the cerebral circulation, are affected during seizure.
seizure is a condition in which CBF and Cyt.ox are increased, and the increased CBF is a compensatory response to the increased metabolic demand of the brain during seizure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cyt.ox.-based monitoring could be used as a useful indicator for the evaluation of brain damage in seizure.
the increase of Cyt. ox. during seizure might be a protective mechanism against the hypoxia caused by the seizure, which might be related to the increase of Cerebral Blood Flow (CBF) in the brain.
the CBF and Cyt.ox., which is a good indicator of the metabolic state of the brain, should be monitored in the brain during and after seizures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the near-infrared spectrometry can be used to measure the oxygenation state in the brain during and after seizures.
the Cyt.ox.-based oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) is an important factor for the determination of the cerebral oxygenation state.
the hemoglobin oxygenation and the redox states of Cyt.oxidase are important in the pathophysiology of seizure.
